 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Zero points, nine assists, no turnovers. Tyler Kolek's night against Orlando needs all three numbers, because leaving any one out would give the Knicks the wrong conclusion.
 His passing earned a follow-up, in my view. Even when Jose Alvarado is available again, I would keep a limited on-ball opportunity for Kolek rather than send him straight back to waiting. The next step can be another brief stretch as an organizer, without handing him the entire backup job after 15 minutes.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Sunday's official box score gives Kolek nine assists in 15:06 without a turnover. It also shows 0-for-4 shooting, including two missed threes, in a 111-102 defeat. He contributed organization without supplying his own scoring, and the Knicks still lost.

Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect
 The Knicks have different jobs available in the backcourt
 Miles McBride's early-season scoring shouldn't make the passing question disappear. He scored 20 points and made six threes against Boston on Friday. He had one assist in that game and one against Orlando, when he finished with a single point.
 Those totals aren't a verdict on everything McBride can do. They show the different contributions New York has received over these particular games. A guard who can finish a possession from outside and a guard who can arrange the pass that creates the shot don't have to be competing for an identical assignment.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Yesterday's McBride analysis argued that his scoring alone couldn't settle the second unit's needs. Kolek has now supplied an actual passing performance to evaluate, rather than merely a theoretical alternative.
 0What do you think? Post a comment. 
 Alvarado missed Sunday's game with a left ankle sprain. His next-game availability isn't established here, and the Knicks don't need to assume a lengthy absence to consider what Kolek offered. They can give him another defined stretch and check whether the offense stays organized against a different opponent.
 The shooting is the obvious test. If defenders stop respecting his attempts, passing lanes can become harder to find. His defensive work also has to support whatever minutes the coaching staff gives him. Nine assists aren't an exemption from those requirements.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement There is a reasonable outcome in which Alvarado and McBride remain the better combination and Kolek returns to a narrower role. Before making that decision, New York has enough evidence to watch him with the ball again. Another modest audition would be a measured response to Sunday, without pretending one scoreless game uncovered a permanent rotation answer.
